title: Reading continuous-time system notation
description: identify $x(t)$ as the input signal and $y(t)$ as the output signal in continuous-time notation.

title: Interpreting the black-box system model
description: interpret a system block as a process that transforms an input signal into an output signal.

title: Describing systems by input-output relationships
description: view system analysis as determining how the output signal depends on the input signal.

title: Recognizing filtering as signal refinement
description: interpret a filter as a system that turns a noisy input into a cleaner output.

title: Mapping physical variables to input and output signals
description: identify which physical quantity plays the role of $x(t)$ and which plays $y(t)$ in a model.

title: Applying Ohm's law in an RC circuit
description: write the resistor current as $(v_s(t)-v_c(t))/R$ from the voltage difference across the resistor.

title: Applying the capacitor current relation
description: write the capacitor current as $C dv_c(t)/dt$ from the capacitor voltage.

title: Deriving the RC circuit differential equation
description: combine the RC current relations and rearrange them into a differential equation for $v_c(t)$ and $v_s(t)$.

title: Modeling retarding force with linear drag
description: represent the automobile's retarding force as $F_r(t)=ρ v(t)$.

title: Applying Newton's second law to automobile motion
description: write the automobile force balance as $F_a(t)-F_r(t)=m dv(t)/dt$.

title: Deriving the automobile differential equation
description: substitute the drag model and rearrange to obtain a differential equation relating $v(t)$ and $F_a(t)$.

title: Converting physical equations to input-output form
description: rewrite equations in variables such as $v_s$, $v_c$, $F_a$, and $v$ using $x(t)$ and $y(t)$.

title: Reading coefficient definitions in system models
description: identify constants such as $a=1/RC$, $b=ρ/m$, and $c=1/m$ from physical parameters.

title: Recognizing first-order system equations
description: identify an input-output differential equation involving the first derivative of the output as first order.

title: Recognizing systems beyond time-domain signals
description: identify that systems can process spatial signals such as images, not only time signals.
